mainTopic: עֶרֶב פֶּסַח: not eating close to מנחה, and how this compares to ערב שבת and ערב יום טוב
overview: The משנה opens פרק ערבי פסחים. On ערב פסח, from close to מנחה time, a person may not eat until dark. Even the poorest Jew must recline at the סדר and must be given four cups of wine. The גמרא asks why the משנה limits the eating rule to ערב פסח, since a ברייתא records רבי יהודה forbidding eating from מנחה onward before every שבת and יום טוב, while רבי יוסי allows eating until dark. רב הונא answers that the משנה follows רבי יוסי, who agrees that on ערב פסח one must stop eating because of the obligation of מצה. רב פפא answers that the משנה can even follow רבי יהודה, because on ערב פסח the ban starts earlier, already close to מנחה. The גמרא challenges רב פפא with another version of the ברייתא, in which רבי יהודה forbids eating on ערב שבת from nine hours. מר זוטרא responds by questioning whether that version is accurate, and his answer continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: No eating on ערב פסח from close to מנחה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that on ערב פסח a person may not eat from close to מנחה time until nightfall.
steps.simpleTranslation: MISHNAH: On ערב פסח, close to מנחה time, a person may not eat until it gets dark.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its first rule: on ערב פסח, from a little before מנחה time, you stop eating and wait until night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The purpose is to come to the סדר hungry, so that the מצה is eaten with appetite. Notice the exact words 'סמוך למנחה', meaning close to מנחה and not only from מנחה onward. The גמרא will build on this wording later.

keyTerms.meaning: Close to מנחה time, a little before it begins

phrases.english: MISHNAH
On the eve of Passover, close to Minchah time,
a person may not eat until it gets dark.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֶרֶב פְּסָחִים סָמוּךְ לַמִּנְחָה לֹא יֹאכַל אָדָם עַד שֶׁתֶּחְשַׁךְ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On ערב פסח, from close to מנחה, one may not eat until dark.
steps.whyThisMatters: The precise words 'סמוך למנחה' become the key to רב פפא's answer later.

steps.title: Even the poorest must recline and get four cups
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds that even a very poor person must recline while eating and must be given four cups of wine, even if he lives on charity.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even the poorest Jew should not eat until he reclines, and they should not give him fewer than four cups of wine, even if he is supported from the community charity plate.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with two more סדר rules: הסיבה (reclining like a free person) and ארבע כוסות, which apply even to the poorest people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stresses that poverty does not excuse anyone from these signs of freedom. The charity collectors must make sure the poor person receives a full four cups. On this עמוד, the גמרא discusses only the first rule, about eating.

keyTerms.meaning: The poorest member of the Jewish people
That he reclines, leaning in the manner of free people
The four cups of wine at the סדר
The community charity plate that gives daily food to the very poor

phrases.english: Even the poorest person in Israel
should not eat until he reclines,
and they should not give him less
than four cups of wine,
even if he is supported from the charity plate.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ עָנִי שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא יֹאכַל עַד שֶׁיָּסֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with more rules for the סדר night
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הסיבה and ארבע כוסות are required even for the poorest Jew.

steps.title: Why only ערב פסח?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה limits the no-eating rule to ערב פסח, since the same seems to apply on ערב שבת and ערב יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: Why does the משנה speak specifically about ערב פסח? The same rule applies on ערב שבת and ערב יום טוב too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's wording. If the rule applies before every שבת and יום טוב, why does the משנה mention only פסח?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack targets the word 'ערב פסחים'. If not eating late in the afternoon is a general rule, then naming פסח alone seems pointless or misleading. The proof for this assumption comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically? A formula asking why a source chose one particular case

phrases.english: GEMARA
Why specifically the eve of Passover?

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ עַרְבֵי שַׁבָּתוֹת וְיָמִים טוֹבִים נָמֵי.
phrases.english: Even on the eves of Shabbat and Festivals it is also so!

steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's limiting of the rule to ערב פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ban on eating late in the day applies before every שבת and יום טוב, singling out פסח seems unnecessary.

steps.title: ברייתא: no eating before שבת and יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי יהודה forbids eating from מנחה onward on ערב שבת and ערב יום טוב, while רבי יוסי allows eating until dark.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: A person should not eat on ערב שבת or ערב יום טוב from מנחה time onward, so that he enters שבת with an appetite. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי says: He may keep eating until it gets dark.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the source behind the question. A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה applies the no-eating rule before every שבת and יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's reason is to arrive hungry, so that the שבת meal is enjoyed. The ברייתא also brings רבי יוסי, who disagrees. That disagreement sets up the two answers that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: Having an appetite or desire to eat

steps.confusionAlert: Only רבי יהודה supports the question. רבי יוסי allows eating on ערב שבת until dark, and רב הונא's answer depends on him.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יֹאכַל אָדָם בְּעַרְבֵי שַׁבָּתוֹת וְיָמִים טוֹבִים
phrases.english: A person should not eat on the eves of Shabbat and Festivals
from Minchah time onward,
so that he enters Shabbat with an appetite;
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Yosei says:
He may continue eating until it gets dark.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the challenge in step 3
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the no-eating rule also applies on ערב שבת and ערב יום טוב
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording רבי יהודה's view (against רבי יוסי)

steps.title: רב הונא: the משנה follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the משנה follows רבי יוסי. He allows eating on ערב שבת but agrees that on ערב פסח one must stop, because of the מצוה of מצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: The משנה is needed only according to רבי יוסי, who said one may keep eating until dark. That applies only on ערב שבת and ערב יום טוב. On ערב פסח, because of the obligation to eat מצה, he agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question. The משנה is teaching that even רבי יוסי, who is lenient before שבת, agrees to stop eating on ערב פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוסי, ערב פסח really is different from ערב שבת. On פסח there is a חיוב דאורייתא to eat מצה, and it should be eaten with appetite. So naming פסח alone is precise: it is the one ערב where רבי יוסי also forbids eating.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for, meaning the source was written for this specific view or case

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
It is needed only according to Rabbi Yosei,
who said: one may continue eating until dark.

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּעַרְבֵי שַׁבָּתוֹת וְיָמִים טוֹבִים,
phrases.english: That applies on the eves of Shabbat and Festivals,
but on the eve of Passover,
because of the obligation of matzah, he agrees.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא לָא צְרִיכָא אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 3 and 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the משנה to the other תנא (רבי יוסי), for whom פסח is unique
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to repeat a rule that applies before every שבת and יום טוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי יוסי, who forbids eating only on ערב פסח, because of the obligation of מצה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the מצוה of מצה creates a stronger reason to stop eating than the general wish to enjoy a שבת or יום טוב meal.

steps.title: רב פפא: even רבי יהודה, the ban starts earlier on פסח
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the משנה can follow רבי יהודה too. Before שבת the ban starts from מנחה, while on ערב פסח it starts even earlier, close to מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: You can even say the משנה follows רבי יהודה. There, on ערב שבת and ערב יום טוב, eating is forbidden only from מנחה onward, and close to מנחה it is permitted. But on ערב פסח, even close to מנחה it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a different answer. Even רבי יהודה treats ערב פסח more strictly, because there the ban begins earlier in the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא reads the משנה's exact words, 'סמוך למנחה', and contrasts them with the ברייתא's 'מן המנחה ולמעלה'. Before שבת, רבי יהודה forbids eating only once מנחה time arrives. On ערב פסח, the ban starts in the period just before מנחה. So the משנה is teaching something new even according to רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say, introducing the idea that a source can fit even a different view

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to 'why only ערב פסח?' According to רב הונא, the משנה follows רבי יוסי, who agrees on פסח because of מצה. According to רב פפא, it can follow רבי יהודה, because on פסח the ban starts earlier, at 'סמוך למנחה' instead of 'מן המנחה'.
steps.confusionAlert: 'סמוך למנחה' (close to מנחה) is earlier than 'מן המנחה ולמעלה' (from מנחה onward). That difference is the whole basis of רב פפא's answer.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
You can even say it follows Rabbi Yehuda.
There, on the eves of Shabbat and Festivals,
it is only from Minchah onward that it is forbidden,
while close to Minchah it is permitted.
But on the eve of Passover,
even close to Minchah it is also forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative answer to רב הונא's in step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the משנה's wording ('סמוך למנחה' compared with 'מן המנחה')
steps.terutzHavaAmina: According to רבי יהודה, the משנה seemed to add nothing beyond the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even according to רבי יהודה, ערב פסח is stricter, because the ban begins close to מנחה rather than at מנחה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Either way, the משנה's focus on ערב פסח is justified.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to forbid eating on ערב שבת from nine hours
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב פפא. A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה as forbidding eating on ערב שבת from nine hours onward, not only from מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really allowed to eat on ערב שבת close to מנחה? But a ברייתא teaches: a person should not eat on ערב שבת and ערב יום טוב from nine hours onward, so that he enters שבת with an appetite. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי says: he may keep eating until dark.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב פפא's answer from the last step. It brings a ברייתא showing that, according to רבי יהודה, the ban on ערב שבת also starts at nine hours.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא said that on ערב שבת the ban starts from מנחה, and on ערב פסח it starts earlier, close to מנחה. This ברייתא says רבי יהודה already forbids eating on ערב שבת from nine hours, which is the same as 'close to מנחה'. If so, ערב פסח is no stricter than ערב שבת, and the משנה's special rule for ערב פסח would again make no sense according to רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Nine hours into the day, a little before מנחה קטנה

steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא looks almost the same as the one in Step 4, but the wording is different. Step 4 said 'from מנחה'. This version says 'from nine hours'. That small change in wording is the whole challenge.

phrases.english: And on Shabbat eve, close to Minchah, it is permitted?
phrases.notes: This refers back to רב פפא's claim that only ערב פסח has a ban close to מנחה.

phrases.english: But it was taught: a person may not eat
on the eve of Shabbat and Festivals
from nine hours onward,
phrases.notes: This is earlier than מנחה קטנה, which begins at nine and a half hours.

phrases.english: so that he enters Shabbat with an appetite,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehudah.
Rabbi Yosei says:
he may keep eating until it gets dark.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבָעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת סָמוּךְ לַמִּנְחָה שְׁרֵי? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step challenges רב פפא's answer in Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that רבי יהודה forbids eating close to מנחה only on ערב פסח, and only from מנחה itself on ערב שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא has רבי יהודה forbidding eating on ערב שבת from nine hours, the same time as ערב פסח. So the difference רב פפא proposed falls apart.

steps.title: מר זוטרא doubts that this version of the ברייתא is accurate
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא pushes back the challenge. Who says this version of the ברייתא, with 'nine hours', is the correct one?
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: Who will tell us that this version is the accurate one?
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא defends רב פפא by questioning the wording of the ברייתא used in the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר זוטרא does not argue with the logic of the challenge. He doubts the text itself. The version in Step 4 said 'from מנחה', and that version fits רב פפא well. Since we cannot be sure the 'nine hours' wording is reliable, it cannot be used to knock down רב פפא's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Who will tell us? A way of doubting an assumption
Accurate or correct, meaning a reliable text version

steps.whatToRemember: On this עמוד, מר זוטרא blocks the challenge to רב פפא by doubting the 'nine hours' version of the ברייתא. The discussion of this wording continues on the next עמוד.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the גמרא sometimes defends a position by questioning the exact wording of a source, rather than by reinterpreting it.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said:
Who will tell us
that it is the accurate version?
phrases.notes: This means the 'nine hours' version of the ברייתא may not be reliable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא: מַאן לֵימָא לַן דִּמְתָרַצְתָּא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step answers the challenge from Step 7 and so protects רב פפא's answer.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof brought in Step 7 from the 'nine hours' version of the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenge relies on a text version whose accuracy is uncertain. The other version says 'from מנחה'.
